findings.evidence: The new comment reads 'THE PATH LIST REPEATS line 770's'. Working tree line 770 is `assert_eq "H.4b error_key=design_rollup_hash_stale" "design_rollup_hash_stale" "$(json_field '.error_key' "$OUT")"` — an assertion with no path list. The repeated list is at line 777 (`epic_review_and_complete "$EPIC" "3" "src/b.sh"`); grep -n 'epic_review_and_complete' returns exactly 656/761/777/938 as call sites. 770 was never correct in any state: in the committed fe278a8 the call sits at 757, and in fe278a8^ there is no "3" call at all (the third call there is "3" "src/a.sh" "src/b.sh" at 904). 757 + the 20 comment lines this round adds = 777.
findings.description: A false cross-reference in a comment whose entire purpose is to let the next reader verify a claimed repetition. The PROPOSITION is true and independently checkable — only two `src/b.sh` path lists exist in the file (761, 777) and they are consecutive calls on the same epic, exactly as the helper contract at 354-370 describes — so a reader lands on the right line within seven lines of the wrong pointer. That is why I grade it medium and not high: nothing about SHIPPED BEHAVIOUR is misstated, and the remedy is one digit. DISCLOSED FOR SYMMETRY, as round 1 disclosed the same thing about R1-F1: if 'makes a shipped claim FALSE' in the operator's stop rule is read to cover any false clause in shipped text rather than only claims about behaviour, this is the one finding in the diff that would be HIGH under that reading, and it is the operator's rule to apply. Fix: 770 -> 777.

findings.evidence: The parenthetical reads: 'An earlier version of this comment blamed G.1's successful approve for TRUNCATING the tracker. That is false: the tracker is non-empty here, and the replacement two steps up is what drops src/a.sh.' Approve DOES truncate the tracker: truncate_changed_files_tracker() at qa-gate.sh:1647-1650 (`: > "$tracking"  # truncate, preserve file`), called from approve's tracking-state finalization (qa-gate.sh:7935-7946, '0wk.2 fix: truncate changed-files.txt - paired with the baseline'). Round 1's suggested wording carried an explicit guard for this — '(G.1's own approve truncates the tracker on success too, but the replacement alone is what produces the miss.)' — which is not in the shipped text.
findings.description: Not a false claim under the supported reading: 'That is false' attaches to the ATTRIBUTION, and the disproof offered ('the tracker is non-empty here') is the right disproof of the attribution rather than of truncation-in-general, so a careful reader reaches the correct conclusion. Graded low because the sentence can still be read as denying a real shipped side effect of qa-gate.sh approve, which is the kind of thing a later reader debugging a change set would act on. One-clause remedy: append 'approve does truncate on success; it is simply not what produces the miss here.'

findings.evidence: The diagnostic ends `| cut -c1-400` with no truncation marker. Measured in situ: I ran the SHIPPED test with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR pointed at a mirror whose workflow-doctor.sh carries DOCTOR_BD_SCHEMA_VALIDATED="9.9.9:99", forcing the 8a control to fail. It printed: 'observed pair (beads detail): bd-version-vs-schema DRIFT: installed bd 1.3.0 / store schema v66 is not in the validated set {9.9.9:99} (bd:schema)' and 'validated set: 9.9.9:99' — ~130 characters, comfortably inside 400, and both lines correct (the pair is this host's real one; the set is the one the failing run actually used, read from the same $DOCTOR the control ran against, not from the repo's canonical copy).
findings.description: Cosmetic and contingent: if the FAIL detail ever grows past 400 characters the operator reads a truncated line as complete, with nothing saying so. Today's detail is a single ~130-char line so it cannot bite. Suggested v5.0.1 polish: append a marker when the cut fires. Everything else about this diagnostic checks out — see the record's own notes for the absent/malformed/jq-failure matrix and the proof it changes no assertion outcome.

Logged so a future reader who finds the two texts disagreeing knows which one the CI record supports, since a commit message cannot be amended in place.
